breaks.why: update_postmeta_cache() runs the native meta functions, whose update_meta_cache() statement selects the id column too (SELECT meta_id, post_id, meta_key, meta_value ...) where WordPress selects SELECT post_id, meta_key, meta_value ..., because the meta entity carries its meta_id. A deliberate difference of phase 3's meta repository (speedyspec-wp-meta-sql's for_objects); the rows, the cache and the query count are WordPress's.

Logging the author in reads the user's meta through the native meta functions, whose update_meta_cache() statement selects the id column too (SELECT umeta_id, user_id, meta_key, meta_value ...) where WordPress selects SELECT user_id, meta_key, meta_value ..., because the meta entity carries its meta_id. A deliberate difference of phase 3's meta repository (speedyspec-wp-meta-sql's for_objects), not of post reading; the wp_count_posts() statement the scenario is about matches in the next step.
